findings.finding: On the artifact, Put stores the flow's value as a JSON STRING: `value: {b: {d: 3}}` (block YAML or flow style) is stored as `"{\"b\":{\"d\":3}}"` (kv() className java.lang.String), and so is an entry list `[{key: x.y, value: 1}]` and even `{{ {'b': 2} }}`. Put.mergeValues is never reached with a Map from a flow. The merge semantics in egret_expected.put_merge come from the artifact's Put.mergeValues run in jshell on typed values. RULED 2026-10-07 by the user: Put stays a real deep merge (egret merges; the artifact's divergence is a spec §2 row).

Every DURATION is stored as an Ion STRING (`"P1D"`, quotes included), not raw ISO bytes: Set coerces DURATION to a validated String, and only a java.time.Duration object (unreachable from the tasks and the API) takes InternalKVStore's raw-bytes branch. Not a stop: it is Ion text. Spec §2/§4.2 amended 2026-10-07.

kvType applies only to a String value (and a Number with STRING becomes its string). A number, boolean, map or list with any other kvType is stored as itself, typed by its own value (t_bool_number stored `true`, BOOLEAN). egret's stored type therefore follows the coerced value (spec §4.2 amended 2026-10-07; review C1: DURATION too, so a stored DURATION is always an Ion string).

Set NUMBER writes a Java Double as Ion float text (`1.5e0`, `1e0`, `100e0`, `1.0e20`, `-1500e0`, `3.141592653589793e0`), an int/long/BigInteger as an Ion int; the API PUT keeps an Ion decimal (`1.5`, `1.50` -> `1.5`, `1.5d0` -> `1.5`). kv() prints a Double as Java's Double.toString (`1.0E20`, `100.0`).

DATETIME is stored as an Ion timestamp at MILLISECOND precision (`.123456789Z` -> `.123Z`), converted to UTC; DATE as a day-precision Ion timestamp (`2025-01-02`). kv() prints Instant.toString; Get's output prints microseconds (`.000000Z`).
A null inside a JSON map is kept in the bytes (`{x:null,y:1}`) but dropped by every read (kv(), Get, API): `{"y":1}`; a null inside a list is kept. egret_expected follows Kestra's read view.

GetKeys and the listings are NOT in byte order: they follow the order in which each key's latest revision was written (Kestra's query has no ORDER BY; a rewrite moves a key to the end). egret: latest revision row id ascending. Spec §8.3 amended 2026-10-07.

No reader answered a live value after expiry (not a stop). Kestra's kv() (errorOnMissing true), Get (both settings) and API GET (410) fail with `The requested value has expired` and SOFT-DELETE the key; kv(..., false) answers null and soft-deletes; GetKeys and the listing skip it without writing; Delete answers deleted: true; the chain shows the first reader changing what the second sees.
Kestra refuses `overwrite: false` over an EXPIRED key (`Key already exists`); egret writes (expired means missing).

PurgeKV `{type: key}` purges revision ROWS whose own expiration passed (ke r2), not every revision of a key whose latest expired; `size` counts revisions. `{type: version}` with neither property purges EVERYTHING (12); `before` with `keepAmount` is refused (`behavior: Cannot set both 'before' and 'keepAmount' properties`); `before` filters on the row's `updated` column (when the revision stopped being latest), not its creation. Spec §2/§8.6 amended 2026-10-07.

PurgeKV's candidate namespaces are the namespaces that have FLOWS (FlowRepository.findDistinctNamespace) filtered by string prefix or wildcard, plus the listed ones: a child namespace with KV but no flow is never purged; with no namespaces every flow namespace of the tenant is purged (31 here). The PurgeKV task log names them (`purging N namespaces: [...]`).

PUT …/kv/{key} parses an Ion STREAM and keeps the FIRST value: `hello world` -> `"hello"`, `1 2` -> `1`, `PT1.5S` -> `"PT1"`. A timestamp at 00:00:00.000Z becomes a DATE; one with an offset is stored as `ZonedDateTime::"…"` (type JSON); `2025-01-01T03:04:05` (no offset) is a 500 that leaves a row with no object; a blob is stored as a blob and read back base64; an s-expression becomes a list; `x::1` falls back to the string. The brief's cells are in egret_expected.api.put_bodies; RULED 2026-10-07 by the user: one Ion value is stored as its type, anything else as the raw text (STRING), and a blob or s-expression is refused 400 naming the type; non_ion, ion_two_values, long_dur, ts_offset_millis, ion_dt_local_like, ion_blob, ion_sexp, ion_timestamp and ts_midnight_millis are chosen accordingly.

Kestra's local storage writes a `{object}.metadata` sidecar per object (`{}` or `{description:…,expirationDate:…}`) and cannot store keys longer than 242 chars (filesystem NAME_MAX 255 with the 13-byte `.ion.metadata` suffix): the row is saved first, so a 350-char key leaves a row with no object. A 351-char key is a DB error (VARCHAR(350)), answered 500.

    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.kv.PurgeKV
    expiredOnly: true
    namespaces:
      - company
    includeChildNamespaces: true
$examples.title: Delete expired keys globally for a specific namespace, with or without including child namespaces.

size.title: The number of purged KV pairs

expiredOnly.title: Delete only expired keys
expiredOnly.description: When true (default), purge removes entries whose `expirationDate` is in the past; otherwise all matched keys are purged.

before.title: The date before which versions should be purged.
before.description: Using this filter will never delete the last version of a KV to avoid accidental full data loss.

keepAmount.title: How much versions should be kept for each matching KV.
keepAmount.description: By default, every matching version is eligible for purge; set `keepAmount` to retain the most recent N per key.
